**Finding submitted — IP: missing (fallback cure proposed).**

- **Investigation:** I read all five sections. Article 1 has HDI designing, developing, hosting and bearing all costs of the Site (p0005–p0007); Article 2 requires the Company to hand over all Content (p0016); Section 5.2 gives the Company artistic/editorial control but no property right (p0032). Searches for ownership, title, proprietary rights, work product and deliverables returned nothing. The only IP-adjacent grant is the narrow, non-exclusive Marks licence in Section 6.1 (p0038–p0039), limited to carrying out HDI's obligations — helpful to us and not flagged. Section 8 is confidentiality only, and Section 10.2's "co-ownership" language concerns the parties' relationship, not IP.
- **Direction:** nothing assigns Company IP or data to HDI, so this is not walk-away; the gap is the absence of any Company licence to the developed Site and any boundary on HDI's use of our Content and data — a genuine fallback failure.
- **Cure:** one insert_after at p0035 adding Section 5.5 carrying exactly the eight fallback elements: HDI retains generic tools and know-how; perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and other deliverables for our business; and HDI's licence in Content or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company limited to processing solely to provide the Services. No survival tail, no assignment demand, no unrelated text touched; redline validated ok:true including the minimality gate.
